summary: The main article describes the use of tert-alkyl oxalate salts as radical precursors for the alkylation of heteroarenes. It includes 5 tables detailing optimization and scope, 1 scheme for the proposed mechanism, and several figures illustrating the general reaction and specific radical precursors.

items.heading: Previous Work
items.caption: Previous Work: tert-Alkyl Oxalate Salts as Radical Precursors, 1,4-Radical Addition
items.description: Shows the previous application of tert-alkyl oxalate salts in 1,4-radical addition reactions (Giese reaction).

items.heading: This Work
items.caption: This Work: tert-Alkyl Oxalate Salts as Radical Precursors, Alkylation of Heterocycles
items.description: Illustrates the general method for alkylating heterocycles using tert-alkyl oxalate salts via photochemical or thermal initiation.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Table 1. Optimization and control reactions for the alkylation of lepidine (1) with oxalate precursor 2.
items.description: Lists various reaction conditions including photocatalyst, oxidant, and temperature to optimize the yield of product 3.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Table 2. Reaction scope of tert-alkyl oxalate salts.
items.description: Displays the variety of tertiary radical precursors (oxalate salts) that can be successfully coupled with lepidine.

items.heading: Table 3
items.caption: Table 3. Reaction scope of heteroarene.
items.description: Shows the scope of different nitrogen-containing heterocycles that can undergo alkylation with the 1-methylcyclohexyl radical.

items.heading: Table 4
items.caption: Table 4. Reaction scope of the alkylation of ligands and biologically-relevant heteroarenes.
items.description: Demonstrates the application of the method to complex ligands like phenanthrolines and bioactive molecules like quinine and fasudil.

items.heading: Table 5
items.caption: Table 5. Reaction scope of the thermal Minisci reaction.
items.description: Compares the yields of the reaction when initiated thermally at 65 °C instead of photochemically.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Scheme 1. Proposed mechanisms for the photoredox-catalyzed Minisci reaction (A) and the thermally initiated Minisci reaction (B) of tert-alkyl oxalate salts.
items.description: Outlines the catalytic cycle for photoredox activation and the radical chain mechanism for thermal activation.
